article_title: PuppyGraph Raises $10M Series A as Its 1.0 Graph Query Engine Adds an AI-Assisted Schema Builder and MCP Integrations

content_preview.title: PuppyGraph Raises $10M Series A as Its 1.0 Graph Query Engine Adds an AI-Assisted Schema Builder and MCP Integrations
content_preview.summary: PuppyGraph, which queries warehouse and lakehouse data as a graph, said it raised $10 million and added an AI-assisted schema builder and MCP integrations; an analyst says the graph model still needs upkeep.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

PuppyGraph, a startup whose query engine lets companies treat data already sitting in warehouses and lakehouses as a single graph, said on November 10, 2026 that it has raised $10 million in new funding, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/10/puppygraph-raises-10m-to-let-ai-agents-query-enterprise-data-as-a-graph/). On the same day, [InfoWorld](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4246810/puppygraph-adds-ai-schema-builder-and-mcp-support-to-help-ease-enterprise...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, funding, release changes, company figures, analyst views, what the sources do not say), 887 words, within the News range of 400-1200. Company statements are consistently labelled as the company's, and the analyst trade-offs are given alongside the vendor claims.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots from disk (sources/2026-11/puppygraph-raises-10m-series-a-as-its-10-graph-query-engine-adds-an-ai-assisted-schema-builder-and-mcp-integrations/): source-0.html.gz (SiliconANGLE, Duncan Riley, updated 09:00 EST 10 Nov 2026, HTTP 200, sha256 df4a5025... re-hashed and matches the manifest) and source-1.html.gz (InfoWorld, Anirban Ghoshal, 10 Nov 2026, HTTP 200, sha256 3dcae285... re-hashed and matches). A live curl with a browser User-Agent also returned HTTP 200 for both URLs. suspicious_patterns is null for both. SiliconANGLE confirms: $10M raised, GTM build-out plus engineering, round follows general release of 1.0, Particle Future and defy.vc led the Series A, defy.vc second lead after a $5M seed in November 2024, $15M total, ARR sevenfold by the startup's count with no dollar figure, Weimo Liu quote verbatim, 3,000 tables and sub-second company claim, 30 to 50 table proof-of-concept framing, own agent plus MCP, bounced queries with agent-actionable errors, short-lived Snowflake/Databricks credentials and row-level checks at each hop (company says), AMD and Palo Alto Networks plus Coinbase, Datadog, Trend Micro named, free Docker download and about 10 minutes to a first query. InfoWorld confirms: Tuesday (10 Nov 2026) announcement, AI-assisted schema builder with review-and-approve, query validation against the schema, distributed execution across nodes (company), LPG model and SQL support, MCP integrations, the ten-customer list, and the Pratt (IDC), Chaturvedi (HFS Research) and Leone (Moor Strategy and Insights) statements; the Pratt, Leone and Chaturvedi quotes are verbatim (the Pratt quote is cut at a clause boundary, the source continues after "joins"). Independence: News article with two independent outlets (SiliconANGLE and InfoWorld, different publishers); the product facts in both rest largely on the company, which the article says. No policy minimum applies to News. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article is not about Anthropic or an Anthropic-operated product and does not name Anthropic; SiliconANGLE mentions Anthropic's Claude only in an investor quote that the article does not use, and MCP appears as a protocol name, not as an Anthropic reference server or product under review. Allowlist: siliconangle.com and infoworld.com already listed; no additions.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy tests run from raw snapshot text. Absence and quantifier sentences: "neither article gives a date for that release" and "neither article gives pricing beyond the free download, the date of the 1.0 general release, or which specific agents and tools the MCP integrations support" hold in both snapshots (InfoWorld's "released in 2024" refers to the earlier engine, not 1.0 GA); "neither article reports an independent benchmark" and "InfoWorld article does not carry [the 3,000-table figures]" hold. Headline, summary and lead keep qualifiers ("said", "according to") and do not rename actors; the Series A label is in SiliconANGLE. Dates: 10 November 2026 matches both (SiliconANGLE "said today" under a 10 Nov update stamp, InfoWorld "on Tuesday", 10 Nov 2026 is a Tuesday). Derived figures: customer list of ten names matches InfoWorld exactly; $5M seed + $10M = $15M matches the outlet. Vendor figures (3,000 tables, sub-second, sevenfold ARR, 10 minutes) are labelled as company claims. Disagreements between sources: none found. Minor looseness, not worth a record: the 30-to-50-table sentence appears in SiliconANGLE's company-argument paragraph without its own attribution, and the article attributes it to the company, which matches the paragraph framing; the last analyst paragraph says "an analyst quoted in the article" where InfoWorld says "the analyst" (Chaturvedi in context), so the vagueness is the source's.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive; no promotional language, trade-offs reported with equal weight.
editor_notes.originality: No prior PuppyGraph coverage in src/content/articles; no recent article covers graph query engines over warehouse data. New topic.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed funding and release coverage with no errors found in headline, summary, lead or body; approve as submitted. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid funding and product news for a data-infrastructure audience, with company-sourced figures and no wider industry significance
